notation.meaning: Point where the curve is evaluated
Span: share of the data in each local window
Distance from $x_0$ to the farthest point in the window
Intercept and slope of a local line

blocks.md: A straight regression line forces one slope on the whole cloud of points. A lowess curve lets the data speak: to draw the curve at any income level, it looks only at the occupations with incomes nearby, gives the closest ones the most weight, fits a short line through them and keeps the height of that line. Sliding the window across the range and joining the heights gives a smooth curve that bends wherever the data bend. Drawn next to the straight line, it shows at a glance whether a straight line is a fair summary or misses a curve.

blocks.title: Why it matters
blocks.md: It is the quickest check of the linearity assumption, on the raw scatterplot before fitting and on the residual plot after.

1. Take the fraction $f$ of observations whose $x_i$ are nearest to $x_0$.
2. Weight them by distance, $w_i = \left(1 - \left|\frac{x_i - x_0}{d}\right|^3\right)^3$, where $d$ is the largest distance in the window (the tricube weight).
3. Fit a line by weighted least squares and record its height at $x_0$:
The curve joins the $\widehat{m}(x_0)$ values. (The steps are the standard algorithm, beyond the lecture, which uses it through seaborn's `lowess=True`.)

sections.heading: Reading it against the OLS line

blocks.md: On the Prestige data the lowess curve (dashed) follows the OLS line up to incomes of about 10,000, then bends below it: prestige rises more slowly at high incomes. A straight line over-predicts prestige for the highest-paid occupations, which suggests a log of income.

blocks.md: With many tied, discrete values (education and vocabulary scores) lowess and OLS nearly coincide: the relationship is close to linear.

blocks.md:
| Span $f$ | Curve | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Large (towards 1) | Smooth, close to a single line | Misses real bends (bias) |
| Small | Follows local detail | Chases noise (variance) |
It is the same trade-off as the bandwidth in [Kernel Density Estimation](note:kernel-density-estimation).

- **Reading the ends.** With few points near the edges, the curve is driven by a handful of observations.
- **Treating it as a model.** Lowess gives no coefficients to interpret; it is a diagnostic for choosing the functional form.

- Econometrics: residual-against-regressor plots (a flat lowess near zero supports linearity) in [Regression Diagnostics](note:regression-diagnostics).
